altText: Ghanaian KG1 children freely exploring crayons, pencils and textured materials while making lines and shapes on large paper.
detailedDescription: In a KG1 classroom, learners use crayons and pencils to draw straight, curved and zigzag lines and simple shapes on large sheets of paper. Some also rub over textured materials to discover rough and smooth surfaces while the teacher encourages free exploration of visual marks and creative play.

altText: KG1 children observing and drawing a cup, shoe, pencil and small plant placed on a classroom table.
detailedDescription: A small group of KG1 learners sits around a low table where a cup, shoe, pencil and potted plant are arranged for close observation. Each child studies the objects carefully before drawing what they see with simple lines and shapes.

figureLabel: Drawing scenes from home and community
altText: KG1 children drawing simple scenes from home and community life such as cooking, walking to school and playing with friends.
detailedDescription: Learners create simple drawings of family and community life, such as helping at home, going to school, playing in a clean compound or visiting the market. The teacher invites them to explain their pictures in their own words and connects drawing with real life experience.

altText: A small group of KG1 children creating one large mural together on a big sheet of paper about their school or community.
detailedDescription: A very large sheet of paper is placed on the floor and a group of KG1 learners works together to draw one big mural of a dream school or healthy community. They share space, contribute different parts of the picture and learn to respect one another’s ideas while making art together.

altText: KG1 children looking at kente cloth and local basket patterns before creating simple repeating designs.
detailedDescription: The teacher shows kente cloth, basket patterns or large pictures of local Ghanaian designs and helps learners notice repeated colours and shapes. Children then create their own simple repeating patterns on paper strips using crayons or coloured pencils.

figureLabel: Recycling art collage from safe materials
altText: KG1 children making collages from clean recycled materials such as cardboard, magazine pieces and fabric scraps.
detailedDescription: KG1 learners use safe recycled materials like cardboard, magazine pieces, clean bottle caps and fabric scraps to build collage pictures. The teacher explains that old materials can be reused creatively instead of becoming waste.

altText: KG1 classroom arranged as a mini gallery while children talk about the artworks they created.
detailedDescription: The classroom is turned into a simple gallery with drawings, paintings and collages displayed neatly on walls and tables. Learners stand by their work, describe what they made and give positive comments about the work of others.

altText: KG1 learners using simple rhythm instruments to play repeated sound patterns together in class.
detailedDescription: KG1 learners sit or stand in a small circle using shakers, tins, sticks or other simple classroom instruments to make repeated sound patterns. The teacher models short rhythmic sequences and the children listen, copy and create their own simple patterns together.

altText: KG1 learners in a singing circle responding to the teacher with simple call-and-response lines.
detailedDescription: Learners gather in a circle and practise simple call-and-response singing with the teacher or a lead child. The activity helps them listen carefully, respond in rhythm and talk about how the performance was made together.

altText: KG1 children using claps, knee taps and gentle stamps to keep a steady beat with a simple rhyme.
detailedDescription: A group of KG1 learners stands in a semi-circle clapping hands, tapping knees and gently stamping feet to keep a steady beat while the teacher chants a short rhyme. The activity helps them listen carefully and stay together in time.

figureLabel: Movement to music fast and slow
altText: KG1 children moving slowly or quickly as music changes from slow to fast.
detailedDescription: In an open space, learners move gently when the beat is slow and more quickly when the beat changes to fast. The teacher uses clear signals and encourages children to listen and respond creatively to tempo changes.

figureLabel: Simple role play of home and school
altText: KG1 children acting out simple home and school scenes with basic props while classmates watch.
detailedDescription: Using simple props such as a bag, book or scarf, learners act out everyday scenes like greeting at home, preparing for school or welcoming classmates. The teacher encourages polite speech and respectful actions through drama.

altText: KG1 children acting out a short drama where friends solve a problem, apologise and make peace.
detailedDescription: A small group of learners performs a short scene where two friends quarrel over a toy, then apologise, shake hands and agree to share. The activity uses drama to practise peaceful conflict resolution in a safe way.

figureLabel: Expressing feelings with voice and face
altText: KG1 children taking turns acting out feelings such as happy and sad using their faces and voices.
detailedDescription: During circle time, learners act out feelings like happy, sad, surprised and afraid using facial expression, posture and simple words. The teacher supports them with a feelings chart and helps them name what they are showing.

figureLabel: Mini performance for class or parents
altText: KG1 children performing a short song or rhyme with actions while classmates or a few parents watch.
detailedDescription: A small group performs a short song, rhyme or movement piece at the front of the classroom while classmates and a few parents or visitors watch. The teacher offers quiet support from the side, helping learners gain confidence before an audience.

altText: KG1 children observing an arts corner with displayed materials, pictures and artworks in the classroom.
detailedDescription: Learners gather around a classroom arts corner where materials, pictures, colours and simple artworks are displayed. They talk about what they see, the tools available and how the space helps them make and appreciate art.

altText: KG1 children discussing repeated shapes, colours and simple patterns in an integrated maths and art activity.
detailedDescription: Learners observe repeated shapes, colours and arrangements in a class activity that combines early maths and art. They point out what they like, notice order and compare visual patterns using simple language.

figureLabel: Story and art about caring for the environment
altText: KG1 children drawing ways to keep their school and community clean after listening to a story.
detailedDescription: After listening to a short story, learners draw themselves putting litter in bins, watering trees or caring for animals and plants. The teacher helps them connect values from the story to visual images in their own drawings.

altText: KG1 children creating simple hats, signs and name tags from paper and recycled materials for classroom drama.
detailedDescription: Before a short drama activity, learners make simple hats, signs or name tags from paper and recycled materials. They later use these props to support role play and discussion in class.

altText: KG1 learners designing a large class poster showing sharing, helping and keeping the classroom tidy.
detailedDescription: On a large shared poster, learners draw caring behaviours such as sharing materials, helping friends and sweeping the classroom. The finished work is designed to be displayed as a visual message for their class community.

altText: A KG1 child and teacher looking through a folder of artworks and discussing one favourite piece.
detailedDescription: In a quiet corner, a child and teacher look through a folder or box of drawings, paintings and collages. The learner chooses a favourite artwork and talks about what was learned from making it.

figureLabel: Identifying colours, sizes and attributes of objects
altText: KG1 children describing objects by colour, size and shape using stones, leaves, cans and classroom materials.
detailedDescription: Learners sort and describe everyday objects such as leaves, stones, empty cans and classroom items using words like red, green, big, small, long and short. Some also compare the attributes of simple three-dimensional objects before drawing them.

figureLabel: Making artworks with colour, shape and simple design
altText: KG1 children creating simple posters, leaf albums and picture rules using different colours and shapes.
detailedDescription: Children use different colours, shapes and pasted leaves to create simple classroom rules posters, warning pictures or small leaf albums. The emphasis is on using the elements of art intentionally to make clear and attractive visual messages.

figureLabel: Talking about art in the natural and manmade environment
altText: KG1 children observing day and night pictures, weather posters and nearby objects while talking about beauty in their environment.
detailedDescription: Learners look at pictures of sunny, rainy and cloudy weather, natural light and simple manmade objects and talk about what looks beautiful or interesting. The activity helps them see art and beauty in both natural and human-made surroundings.

figureLabel: Discussing artworks and performances from our culture
altText: KG1 children looking at pictures of festivals, cloth, drums and other Ghanaian cultural artworks and performances.
detailedDescription: The teacher shows pictures of cloth patterns, festival scenes, drums and other artworks or performances from Ghanaian culture. Learners talk about what they notice and begin to connect art with culture, celebrations and everyday life.

altText: KG1 learners singing, clapping and dancing to a Ghanaian song while using simple shakers and improvised instruments.
detailedDescription: Learners sing a traditional or patriotic Ghanaian song, clap in rhythm and move together while a few children play simple shakers or improvised instruments. The scene shows dance and music inspired by Ghanaian history and culture in a child-friendly way.
